name: Adversarial Threat Landscape for Artificial-Intelligence Systems
owner: MITRE Corporation (Center for AI Security collaboration)
description: MITRE ATLAS is the AI-specific counterpart to ATT&CK: a globally-accessible, ATT&CK-style matrix of adversary tactics and techniques targeting machine learning systems. ATLAS covers techniques such as ML Model Reconnaissance, Resource Development (adversarial ML capabilities), Initial Access (against ML systems), ML Attack Staging, Model Evasion, Inference, Exfiltration, and Impact. Built on observations of real-world attacks plus academic adversarial ML research. The framework is companion to MITRE ATT&CK — many ATLAS techniques reference ATT&CK techniques where relevant, and the case studies section documents real incidents (model evasion attacks on commercial AI services, adversarial-example exploitation of ML classifiers, training-data poisoning, etc.).
relationToCloudSecurity: ATLAS overlaps with cloud security where AI/ML systems are hosted in cloud environments: model APIs (Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Vertex AI), MLOps pipelines, and training infrastructure are all in scope. ATLAS techniques inform threat models for cloud-hosted AI services.
relationToAISecurity: ATLAS is THE leading framework for adversarial ML threat modeling. Direct counterpart to CSA AICM (which catalogs controls); ATLAS catalogs threats. Used together: ATLAS for what adversaries do, AICM/AI RMF for what to do about it.

license.notes: The atlas-data GitHub repository is published under Apache-2.0. Both the data (YAML) and any derived structured forms are freely redistributable; preserve MITRE attribution and the Apache-2.0 LICENSE.

lifecycle.notes: Actively maintained on monthly calendar-versioned releases. Versioning switched from semver to CalVer: v5.6.0 (2026-05-04) was the last semver release, followed by v2026.05, v2026.06, v2026.07 (published 2026-08-07, dated 2026-07-31). Schema format-version 6.0.0 accompanied the switch; releases 2026.02 through 2026.04 shipped both v6 and 5.x, and from 2026.05 onward it is v6 only. Pin to a specific tag for reproducibility.

current_extraction.notes: Reference-only. Corrected 2026-08-12: this entry previously pointed at dist/ATLAS.yaml as the primary file. That path still exists but is 5.x-era sized (452 KB vs 717 KB for 2026.07) and is NOT a safe pointer. Upstream reorganized dist/ when format-version 6.0.0 landed: dist/v6/ATLAS-<CalVer>.yaml is the current line, dist/legacy/ATLAS-<semver>.yaml holds the frozen 5.x line, and dist/manifest.yaml is a machine-readable release-to-path index. Prefer manifest.yaml over any hardcoded path — it survives the next dist/ reshuffle. Consumers should pull from upstream by tag.

scope.release_pattern: GitHub releases, CalVer monthly (currently v2026.07). Switched from semver after v5.6.0.
scope.covers: 1 matrix, 16 tactics, 101 techniques + 77 sub-techniques, 37 mitigations, 68 case studies (counts as of 2026.07)
scope.identifier_pattern: AML. prefix throughout: AML.TA#### (tactic), AML.T####[.###] (technique/sub-technique), AML.M#### (mitigation), AML.CS#### (case study). Dots preserved in URLs, unlike ATT&CK sub-techniques.
scope.identifier_stability: WEAK — ATLAS provides no deprecation mechanism. Verified 2026.04 to 2026.07: AML.T0019, AML.T0058 and AML.T0104 were deleted outright (folded into AML.T0115 sub-techniques) with no revoked-by, no deprecated flag, and no redirect; the mapping exists only in upstream CHANGELOG prose. The STIX bundle carries zero revoked/x_mitre_deprecated objects. Object uuid fields are UUIDv5 (deterministic name-based hashes), so they change by construction on rename or re-parent and cannot serve as permanent keys — all three retired techniques' UUIDs are absent from 2026.07, while the 167 IDs present in both releases showed zero UUID drift. Cite ATLAS objects WITH a release, e.g. 'AML.T0115.000 @ 2026.07'. Tracked in SecID issue #155.
scope.stix_channel: mitre-atlas/atlas-navigator-data (dist/stix-atlas.json, plus Navigator layers and OpenCTI bundles) — lags atlas-data by a release or more; had 170 attack-patterns (the 2026.04 snapshot) when checked on 2026-08-12.

notes: Reference entry. ATLAS upstream at mitre-atlas/atlas-data is the canonical source — pin to a release tag for reproducibility. Note the repo is no longer data-only: it now also ships a Python API package under atlas/ (routes.py, models.py, db/, services/).
